rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior surah's close warns readers not to become like Abu Lahab, ruined and entering the Fire, even if their apparent condition suggests otherwise.
rows.anchor: وختمها إشارة إلى التحذير من مثل حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar establishes the Prophet's special good and that his hater is cut off; al-Kafirun then permits peaceful separation while believers are few.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الكوثر علة للنهي عما تضمنه التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nasr teaches that victory needs no inquiry about its timing; the proper response when it comes is worshipful gratitude, since its arrival is certain.
rows.anchor: فجاءت سورة النصر لذلك الإشارة إلى أنه مما لا يسأل عنه بمتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's close kinship did not prevent intense hostility to the Prophet, prompting the question whether he would repent or suffer final loss.
rows.anchor: استحضرت حال أبي لهب لما كان فيه مع قرابته القريبة من شدة العناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called al-Asas, al-Muqashqishah, and Qul Huwa Allah Ahad; it establishes God's unique perfection, sound belief, and pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: وتسمى الأساس والمقشقشة وقل هو الله أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its purpose is to affirm perfection and remove every blemish of deficiency, producing good speech and deeds and steadfast reliance in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: بإثبات الكمال ، ونفي الشوائب النقص والاختلال

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon calls al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas the two al-Muqashqishatan because they free people from hypocrisy and shirk, like a treatment that clears scabies.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس : المقشقشتان الكافرون والإخلاص

rows.speaker: عبد الحق
rows.claim: Abd al-Haqq compares the surahs' purifying effect to a sick person recovering from an illness.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام عبد الحق في كتابه الواعي : كما يبرئ المريض من علته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Muqashqishah is connected to gathering: the surahs gather and remove kinds of hypocrisy, shirk, and unbelief from a reader who recites them rightly.
rows.anchor: وهو مأخوذ من القش بمعنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qul Huwa Allah Ahad signals the surah's purpose, and the surah is the Qur'an's greatest exposition of monotheism.
rows.anchor: وهذه السورة أعظم مفيد للتوحيد في القرآن

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says verbal expression cannot encompass monotheism: speaking of the Real entails a speaker, what is spoken of, and the report, while intellect can grasp it.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : والتوحيد مقام يضيق عنه نطاق النطق

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd defines monotheism as a state in which forms disappear, knowledge becomes perplexed, and God remains as He always was.
rows.anchor: سئل الجنيد عن التوحيد ققال : معنى تضمحل فيه الرسوم

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd calls Abu Bakr's declaration the noblest word on monotheism: creatures can know God only by recognizing their inability to know Him.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد أيضا : أشرف كلمة في التوحيد ما قاله الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as possessing all majesty and beauty, extending favors to all beings, and completing grace for those devoted to Him.
rows.anchor: الذي له جميع الكمال بالجلال والجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah sequence moves from al-Kawthar's assurance of the Prophet's good, through peaceful dissociation in al-Kafirun and certain victory in al-Nasr, to Abu Lahab's fate.
rows.anchor: ولما ظهرت ذخائر هذه الكنوز بدقائق تلك الرموز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's misery brought him down through Hell's levels and barred him from rising to the highest ranks.
rows.anchor: فجاءت سورته لذلك بينا لأنه غلب عليه الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah declares the Prophet's fiercest enemy and his wife irreparably doomed to the lowest humiliation and greatest loss.
rows.anchor: فحكم بهلاكه ، وهلاك زوجه هلاكا لا جبر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ikhlas follows by disclosing the majesty of the Lord who commanded the religion and enabled events beyond human power, so nothing is impossible for Him.
rows.anchor: جاءت الإخلاص كاشفة لما ثبت من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's surah sequence from al-Fil onward unfolds the themes of al-Fatiha and then reaches the call to worship in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: أنه سبحانه شرح بالفيل وما بعدها من السور آيات الفاتحة كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fil points to God's perfection through protection of His House, defense from tyrants, and care for Quraysh and Mecca; this points to His judgment of creation.
rows.anchor: بالفيل إلى استجماعه لصفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara depicts believers entering the faith while Abu Lahab and those like him remain impervious to warning and face ruin under the One who commands worship.
rows.anchor: وأعتاهم سواء عليهم الإنذار وعدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the surah of divine perfection completes the account of God's attributes, the two protecting surahs close the sequence against spiritual lapse.
rows.anchor: فختم بالمعوذتين لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ikhlas reveals the greatness of the Lord who commanded the religion and accomplished what lies beyond human power, so no act is impossible for Him.
rows.anchor: جاءت الإخلاص كاشفة لما ثبت من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah's placement completes a sequence in which al-Fil and the following surahs unfold al-Fatiha, then al-Baqara's call to worship.
rows.anchor: شرح بالفيل وما بعدها من السور آيات الفاتحة كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fil signifies God's perfection by protecting the Sacred House and nurturing Quraysh and Mecca, thereby pointing to His judgment of all people.
rows.anchor: بما حرس من بيته من الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara contrasts those guided into faith with Abu Lahab and other unresponsive disbelievers, whose ruin follows God's command to worship and affirm unity.
rows.anchor: وأعتاهم سواء عليهم الإنذار وعدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualities in this surah complete the religion's account of God's majesty and perfection; the closing pair then protects believers from error.
rows.anchor: فتم الدين عند ذلك بما له سبحانه من كمال الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an invites people to God, so it must make Him known through His essence, attributes, and acts; this final community receives the fullest account in scripture.
rows.anchor: وكان التعريف تارة للذات وتارة للصفات وتارة للأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing God's essence is exceptionally difficult; revelation generally uses hints of absolute transcendence and majesty, including the denial of likeness.
rows.anchor: لأن القرآن لا يشتمل من ذلك إلا على تلويحات وإشارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah gives the fullest possible human account: God alone has unchanging existence, without likeness, equal, spouse, child, or need, and controls creation and command.
rows.anchor: ببيان أنه ثابت ثباتا لا يشبهه ثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening command “Say” identifies Muhammad's messengership and answers both his personal deniers and Brahmins who claim reason makes messengers unnecessary.
rows.anchor: ردا على من كذبه في خاصة نفسه وعلى البراهمة القائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted command makes the message universal, addressing anyone who could ask, whether actually or potentially, and rejects restricting his mission to Arabs.
rows.anchor: ففي الإطلاق المشير إلى التعميم رد على من أقر بإرساله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's plain meanings are accessible and harmless; spiritual danger comes when misguided readers probe beyond what their minds can bear.
rows.anchor: وإنما تأتي الفتنة عند تعمق الضال إلى ما لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is directed especially against those who deny God, including people who say that life and death are governed only by time.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أهم المقاصد الرد على المعطلة الذين هم ضرب ممن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah answers deniers who attribute life and death to time, affirming God's existence with the greatest certainty.
rows.anchor: أثبت وجوده سبحانه على أتم الوجوه وأعلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “He” is addressed to those who perceive hidden realities and indicates God's necessary existence, whose identity depends on nothing else.
rows.anchor: فابتدأ بهذا الاسم الشريف الذي هو أبطن الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God remains Himself whether or not anything else is considered; anything whose identity depends on another would cease to be itself without that other.
rows.anchor: فمتى لم يتعبر غيره فلم يكن هو هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun's hāʾ, articulated in the deepest throat, signals God as first and hidden; its wāw, articulated at the lips, signals last and manifest.
rows.anchor: إلى أنه هو الأول والباطن المبدع لما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters also suggest that God is the ultimate end, origin and restorer, and that He encompasses all things.
rows.anchor: وأن إليه المنتهى , وليس وراءه مرمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God's existence is self-subsisting, He cannot be defined through genus, species, difference, or cause; a causeless essence is known through its implications.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا جنس لا ولا نوع له ولا سبب يعرف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an uncomposed essence, the fullest definition combines negative and relational attributes, especially those nearest to the essence.
rows.anchor: وبالجمع بين السلبية والإضافية أتم من الاقتصار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the greatest name is the last of the manifest names and the first among the hidden names.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الاسم الأعظم آخر الظواهر من الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Allah” names the true existent, comprehends all names of perfection and all meanings of the beautiful names, and is the nearest implication of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: واختير هذا الاسم للإخبار عنه لدلالته على جميع صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name combines necessary existence with God's voluntary bestowal of existence on everything He wills, thereby expressing divinity.
rows.anchor: بواسطة وجوب وجوده كان مفيضا باختياره الإيجاد على كل شيء أراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Allah indicates there is no constituent or cause in His essence and that His divinity extends to all beings.
rows.anchor: ودل التعبير به على أنه لا مقوم للهوية من جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Near implications can fully define an uncomposed essence, as constituents define a composite; a true definition produces a matching mental conception.
rows.anchor: تعريف ما لا تركب فيه باللوازم القريبة في الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next negative name gives special weight to divine majesty and absolute unity, excluding every share or multiplicity and implying that all else is nothing beside God.
rows.anchor: فقال مكاشفا للقلوب وللعارفين مكذبا للنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affirmation of God's unity refutes Christian trinitarianism, Jewish corporealism, Zoroastrian dualism, Sabian star-worship, and idol worship.
rows.anchor: وللصابئة الذين يعبدون النجوم , وللمشركين القائلين بإلهية الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ahad” can be parsed as a second predicate, an appositive to Allah, or a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: أو مبدلا من الجلالة , أو مخبرا عن مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In affirmative use, Ahad is uniquely God's name and needs no definite article; it indicates majesty more deeply, while Allah more deeply indicates perfection.
rows.anchor: وهو لأجل كونه خاصة في الإثبات حال الانفراد به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True oneness excludes composition, bodily location, partners in essence, and shared divine properties such as necessary existence and perfect power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: ما يكون منزه لاذات عن أنحاء التركيب والتعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readings omit “Say” from this surah and the two protecting surahs; the author explains the variation by their different rhetorical purposes.
rows.anchor: بإسقاط ( قل ) هنا وفي المعوذتين مع الاتفاق على إثباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Say” suits al-Kafirun's direct address to disbelievers; its omission suits the rebuke of the Prophet's uncle in al-Masad, while other surahs command proclamation or supplication.
rows.anchor: الكافرون مخاطبة للكفار بما بين مشاققة ومتاركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's divinity precedes Ahad because divinity entails self-sufficiency and the dependence of all; a composite would need its parts, whereas unity alone does not entail divinity.
rows.anchor: لأن الإلهية عبارة عن استغنائه عن الكل , واحتياج الكل إليه

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Avicenna argues that indivisibility in thought is a stronger form of unity than divisible unity, and sensory potential division is weaker still.
rows.anchor: قال ابن سينا - مقول على ما تحته بالتكشيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad is chosen over Wahid to express maximal unity: God has no intellectual or physical parts, matter, form, accidents, limbs, shape, color, or other duality.
rows.anchor: والأحد جامع لذلك دال على الواحدية من جميع الوجوه

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Iqlici reports differing etymologies: some treat Ahad as a form of Wahid with a dropped alif or substituted hamza; others derive it separately from Wahd.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو العبا الإقليشي في شرح شرح الأسماء

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: Among those distinguishing the words, some regard Ahad as an independent form, while others derive it from Wahd with waw replaced by hamza.
rows.anchor: وأما من فرق بينهما فمنهم من قال : أحد اسم على حياله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drawing on commentaries by al-Razi and al-Harali, the author says Wahid denies every kind of multiplicity and duplication while affirming greatness.
rows.anchor: وقد استخلصت الكلام على الأسمين الشريفين من عدة شروح

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: True unity belongs only to what has no parts; applying it to a man or coin is figurative, and a created indivisible atom still differs from its Creator.
rows.anchor: فلا يصح أن يوصف شيء مركب بها إلا مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is absolutely One: the created atom's existence depends on another, unlike its Maker, and true unity also excludes any counterpart.
rows.anchor: علمت أن استحقاقه لهذا الوصف ليس كاستحقاق موجده له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unity also means that God acts and creates independently, without needing a partner, adviser, or any other cause; reason and revelation establish this.
rows.anchor: مستبد بالفعل مستقل بالإيجاد ومتوحد بالنصع متفرد بالتدبير

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali defines Ahad as having no counterpart and Wahid as neither divisible nor duplicated; only the eternal One has an existence no other could share.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام حجة الإسلام أبو حامد الغزالي

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: A human may be called one only relative to peers, a time, or a particular virtue; absolute unity belongs only to God.
rows.anchor: والعبد إنما يكون واحدا إذا لم يكن له في أبناء جنسه نظير

rows.speaker: الشهرستاني
rows.claim: Al-Shahrastani distinguishes one as a unit composing a number, its cause outside the count, or a quality predicated of counted things; none describes God exactly.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام محمد بن عبد الكريم الشهرستاني في مقدمة كتابه

rows.speaker: الشهرستاني
rows.claim: God is One unlike numerical units: multiplicity derives from Him, and division is impossible for Him in every sense.
rows.anchor: فهو واحد لا كالأحاد أي هذه الوحدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is One in Himself, not by comparison with a second being.
rows.anchor: وهو واحد أيضا بنفسه لا بالنسبة إلى ثان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One signifies eternity and priority as the basis of number, while Ahad signifies God's separation from creation in every attribute and the denial of all forms of shirk.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الواحد يدل على الأزلية والأولية

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim cites a philosopher: God was eternally One before creation, while created beings depend on Him and on one another; He needs nothing and has no rival.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام بأو حاتم محمد بن مهران الرازي في كتابه الزينة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: The philosopher says God's priority proves His unity: as one precedes and lies outside numerical count, the One is the source of all and depends on none.
rows.anchor: والأولية دلت على الوحدانية

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: The philosopher concludes that God has neither predecessor nor successor and is therefore both Wahid and Ahad.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم يكن قبله شيء ولا بعده شيء فهو المتوحد بالأزل

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: The philosopher says Ahad is broader than Wahid: denying that one can oppose someone may still allow two or more, but denying Ahad excludes every number.
rows.anchor: فصار الأحد أكمل من الواحد

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: In ordinary usage Wahid can include humans, animals, or other things, whereas Ahad is specific to human beings and cannot enter arithmetic.
rows.anchor: فكان الواحد يعم الناس وغير الناس

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: The report explains that Ahad cannot be counted, multiplied, or divided, while Wahid participates in numerical operations and can be a part of a larger number.
rows.anchor: والأحد ممتنع من هذا

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: God truly bears both names: He existed before any second being, while created things are called one only by ordinary wording despite their composition and multiplicity.
rows.anchor: وقد سمى الله نفسه واحدا أحدا ووصف نفسه بالوحدانية والأحدية

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: God is the sole originator, with nothing before Him, from Him, within Him, or beside Him as a second; created things belong to Him.
rows.anchor: بل هو الواحد منشئ والأشياء كلها له

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Created beings' apparent oneness is only lexical because each comprises multiple substances or qualities and bears plurality, opposition, and division.
rows.anchor: والمسمى لا يخلو من معان كثيرة مجتمعة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family of Arabic forms for one all derives from the root of unity; al-Wahid and al-Ahad are the forms used for God.
rows.anchor: وفي الواحد عن العرب لغات كثيرة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Ahad may mean first or one in affirmative statements; the weekday Sunday is called al-Ahad because it is the first day, with Monday named second.
rows.anchor: والأحد يجئ في الكلام بمعنى الأول وبمعنى الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests Sunday may be called God's day because it was the first day created, after which Monday was named the second day.
rows.anchor: قلت : يمكن أن يكون معنى يوم الأحد يوم الله

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Ahad contrasts with al-akhar, as in the report of one prisoner's dream followed by the other's dream.
rows.anchor: قال أحدهما أراني أعصر خمرا

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: If Ahad means first, it can appear in both affirmative and negative speech; if it means one, it can be affirmed as in the command to send one person.
rows.anchor: فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: When Ahad means neither first nor one, it is used only in negation, as in the claim that no one can overpower a person.
rows.anchor: أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Ahad is grammatically invariant for masculine and feminine, unlike Wahid, which takes a feminine form; the cited verse applies it to women.
rows.anchor: يا نساء النبي لستن كأحد من النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad can also convey a collective meaning in Arabic; in theology Wahid is a positive relational attribute, whereas Ahad comprehensively denies number and composition.
rows.anchor: فالواحد من الأسماء الثبوتية الإضافية

rows.speaker: الزويني
rows.claim: Al-Zuwayni transmits views that Ahad negates what follows it and that God cannot be divided either in fact or imagination; God is one in essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو الخير الزويني الشافعي

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says God is One in essence, attributes, and acts, indivisible and uncomposed, incomparable, without equal, and independent of all.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين الرازي في شرح الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's own monotheistic declaration is His knowledge and report that He is One; a servant's monotheism is knowing and affirming this.
rows.anchor: وتوحيد الله تعالى لنفسه علمه بأنه واحد

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thalab distinguishes the terms by saying Wahid can enter number, but Ahad cannot; Ahad is therefore specifically divine.
rows.anchor: أنه فرق بينهما بأن واحدا يدخله العدد

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says Ahad is exclusive to God, whereas the name Wahid can be shared with created beings.
rows.anchor: إنه اختص به البارئ سبحانه , أما الواحد فيحصل فيه المشاركة

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari reports Ahmad ibn Yahya rejecting a plural of Ahad, while allowing Ahad to be understood as a plural of Wahid like ashhad from shahid.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري : سئل أحمد بن يحيى عن الأحاد

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Iqlici says Ahad names the essence and excludes multiplicity; it therefore distinguishes God from bodies and from created indivisible points or substances.
rows.anchor: وقال الإقليشي في شرح الأسماء : الأحد هو الذي ليس بمنقسم

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: A point is an accident at a line's end, an atom is measured and bears accidents, and a philosopher's simple substance distinguishes existence from essence; each differs from God.
rows.anchor: أما النقطة فعرض عند بعضهم إذ هي عبارة عن طرف الخط

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Iqlici contrasts Wahid, which denies partner and equal outside the essence, with Ahad, which concerns the essence itself.
rows.anchor: وأما الواحد فهو وصف لذاته , فيه سلب الشريك والنظير عنه

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi argues that anything worshipped beside God cannot be divine because it has signs of origination, divisibility, and finitude, unlike the Creator.
rows.anchor: وقال البهقي في كتاب الأسماء والصفات : الأحد فيما يدعوه المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad is inherently definite whether written with or without the article, answering the objection that an indefinite word cannot modify the definite name Allah.
rows.anchor: إنه لا فرق في إطلاقه عليه سبحانه وتعالى بين تعريفه وتنكيره

rows.speaker: صاحب كتاب الزينة
rows.claim: The author of the Book of Adornment says the community agreed on the recitation with Ahad indefinite.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب كتاب الزينة : وعلى هذه القراءة - أي قراءة التنكير - أجمعت الأمة

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Some people transmit a recitation from Ja'far al-Sadiq that adds al-Wahid and repeats al-Ahad before al-Samad.
rows.anchor: وروى قوم عن أبي عبد الله بن جعفر بن محمد الصادق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says Arabs used Ahad in its real sense only in negation, since human reason can grasp its universal scope negatively but not affirmatively.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو الحسن الحرالي في شرح الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali calls the surah one of the Qur'an's three lights, welcomed by believers because it gathers uncountable praise of the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وهي أحد الأنوار الثلاثة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents the Qur'an as a light, with al-Ikhlas at its end, Ayat al-Kursi at its beginning, and Yasin in its place before it.
rows.anchor: ونور نوره سورة ذكر الأحد في ختمه وآية الكرسي في ابتدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad comprehensively excludes any other being, while Ilah may be falsely pluralized because it stands in relation to a second.
rows.anchor: وهو واحد مبين عن اسم الإله الذي لا يصح فيه الشرك حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since all creatures perish and remain within God's grasp, nothing exists as an equal or external counterpart to Him.
rows.anchor: فإن الخلق فان فهو في الحقيقة عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects pantheist inference from the discussion, saying the surrounding context leaves no room for the people of unity to claim their doctrine.
rows.anchor: هذا مراده بدليل سابقه ولاحقه فلا شبهة فيه لأهل الوحدة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the range of realities from ultimate unity through lesser degrees is encompassed by Ahadiyya, from which nothing escapes.
rows.anchor: وجماع إحاطات كل ذلك أعلى وأدنى هي الأحدية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Some divine names are known to created representatives, some are beyond their full comprehension, and Ahad is beyond what intellect can attain.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما لم ينله العلم ولا أدركت مثله العقول وهو اسمه الأحد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Ahad denotes pure unity and is used in negation to exclude both even and odd numbers; Wahid loses its singularity when another is joined to it.
rows.anchor: لأن واحدا تزول عنه الواحدية بضم ثان إليه

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some gnostics describe the divine essence as pure hidden unity, with Ahad as its first determination, followed by divinity and then Wahid.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين في كشف معنى الأحد ورتبته

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: The gnostic sequence links Wahid to understanding God, Ilah to understanding Ahad, and Ahad to worship of the most holy essence.
rows.anchor: فإن الواحد مرقى إلى فهم الإله , والإله مرقى إلى تعقل الأحد

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Belief in God's absolute oneness yields love and reverence, since exclusive unity entails perfection and beauty.
rows.anchor: ومن اعتقد أحديته سبحانه وتعالى , أنتج له ذلك حبه وتعظيمه

rows.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr says that after the Qur'an completes its purpose, it reminds the world that created people pass between two states of nonexistence.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام جعفر بن الزبير : لما انقضى مقصود الكتاب العزيز

rows.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Created existence comes from God and is sustained by Him; every creature and all its words and deeds are His creation.
rows.anchor: فوجودهم منه سبحانه وبقاؤهم به

rows.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: God existed before world, time, and place and remains as He was, needing no helper and being confined by neither time nor place.
rows.anchor: وقد كان سبحانه وتعالى ولا عالم ولا زمان ولا مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves praise and possesses judgment, and to Him is the final return; He is true existence and His speech is true.
rows.anchor: له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة , وله الحكم وإليه المصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for the God-fearing than the present world's diversion and play.
rows.anchor: والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed person reads God's signs clearly, understands self and worldly life, answers God's call, and sees Him as the only true agent.
rows.anchor: أجاب داعي الله ولم ير فاعلا في الوجود حقيقة إلا هو

rows.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr says that after the Qur'an's purpose is complete, reflective people should seek refuge from envious people and enemies, as the two protecting surahs do.
rows.anchor: فختم بالمعوذتين من شر ما خلق وذرأ وشر الثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having reached its fullest expression, the discourse ends its account of the divine essence with Ahad, which excludes division and counterpart.
rows.anchor: وكان الأحد من النعوت المتوغلة في السلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next sentence omits a conjunction because it follows as the conclusion and proof of the previous one, addressing believers and scholars directly.
rows.anchor: وأخلى الجملة عن عاطف لأنها كالنتيجة للأولى والدليل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine name is repeated rather than replaced with a pronoun so readers do not mistake God's description as restricted to an aspect or state.
rows.anchor: معيدا الاسم ولم يضمر لئلا يظن تقيد بحيثية غيب أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samad means absolute lordship and perfection: God needs nothing, all things need Him, and all needs are directed to Him; He has no cavity or composition.
rows.anchor: فكان بحيث لا يحتاج إلى شيء وكل شيء إليه محتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The observed world's composition shows it is contingent, so it requires an eternal necessary creator; God's power and choice created it, not natural compulsion.
rows.anchor: فكان موجدا للعالم لأن العالم مركب بدليل المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If creation followed nature, cause and effect would be co-eternal, making either the world eternal or God originated, an impossibility.
rows.anchor: لو كان بالطبع والإيجاب لكان وجوده مع وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text emphasizes that only God is al-Samad because creatures' pressing dependence can obscure His exclusive self-sufficiency; Ahad's exclusivity is self-evident or gently deferred.
rows.anchor: ولم يقصر الأحدية إما للتنبيه على أن ذلك لشدة ظهوره غني عن التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars derive al-Samad from intending or turning to someone: God is the master to whom all appeal, a uniquely fitting and unshared name.
rows.anchor: والصمد من صمد إليه - إذا قصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samad also means without a cavity or softness; hollows need containers, while a solid, smooth stone admits and releases nothing.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا الذي لا جوف له ولا رخاوة بوجه فيه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the dāl in ṣamad substitutes for tāʾ, making the word equivalent to al-muṣmat, solid or closed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : وهو على هذا الدال فيه مبدله من التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samad can also mean exalted or elevated, as Arabs call a hill above the ground ṣamad and describe a built mound as elevated.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا العالي الذي تناهى علوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, God is master of every being, which depends on Him for its origin and care and turns to Him for every need.
rows.anchor: والكل محتاجون إليه في ابتداء إيجادهم وفي تربيتهم

rows.speaker: الإقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Iqlici says that interpreting al-Samad as the one relied upon yields attributes of lordship such as generosity and forbearance; interpreting it as exalted yields might and dominion.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا أي أنه الذي يلجأ إليه ويعتمد عليه لتناهي سؤدده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits Ibn Abbas's description of al-Samad as the master complete in nobility, greatness, forbearance, wealth, might, knowledge, judgment, and every honor.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله ( الصمد ) قال : هو السيد الذي كمل في سؤدده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas concludes that this complete description belongs only to God, who has no equal and nothing like Him.
rows.anchor: هذه صفته لا تنبغي إلا له , ليس له كفوء

rows.speaker: ابن تيمية
rows.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says the early community agreed God is distinct from creation and described only by revealed perfections, without distortion, denial, specifying how, or likeness.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العباس بن تيمية الحنبلي في كتابه ( الفرقان بين أولياء الرحمن وأولياء الشيطان ) : أجمع سلف الأمة وأئمتها أن الرب سبحانه وتعالى بائن منمخلوقاته

rows.speaker: ابن تيمية
rows.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says God has no equal in any perfection attribute and is unlike all things.
rows.anchor: ونعلم أنه ليس كمثله شيء ولا كفوء له في شيء من صفات الكمال
